newsitem.title: USA: Etown Gas proposes "shop around" service.
newsitem.headline: Etown Gas proposes "shop around" service.

text.p: Elizabethtown Gas Co said Thursday it has proposed offering residential customers in seven communities the ability to buy their natural gas from someone other than Elizabethtown.

The NUI Corp division said it filed a proposal with the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities for a two-year pilot program that will allow a group of residential customers to purchase their natural gas from third party suppliers.

Under the proposed program - Elizabethtown Plus -- the utility's residential customers in Clark, Cranford, Garwood, Roselle, Roselle Park, Westfield and Winfield Park will be eligible for the pilot program, which is slated to begin in November.

Under an existing program, about 1,200 of Elizabethtown's 16,000 commercial and industrial customers currently use transportation service from the utility, buying the natural gas from other parties, it said.
Elizabethtown said it is limiting participation in the residential program to 5,000 customers in the first year and an additional 5,000 in year two.
Under the proposal, third party suppliers will be required to sign up a minimum of 50 customers.
